name: Arts and Crafts Jewellery
aliases: Hand-made studio jewels of the Arts and Crafts movement
summary: Hand-made jewels of silver, enamel and soft stones, from the guilds and studios of Britain after 1890. They show visible hammer marks, wire work and cabochons in place of the bright, cut stones of the shops.

philosophy.core_thesis: A jewel is a piece of craft. The maker's hand, a modest metal and a soft stone count for more than the weight of the gold.
design_principles: Make each piece by hand from a drawing of your own, and leave the hammer marks and the file marks on the metal.
Choose silver, copper and low-carat gold in place of platinum and large diamonds.
Set cabochon stones such as moonstone, opal, turquoise and amethyst in a plain bezel.
Use enamel in small areas of blue, green and white, fired on silver or gold.
Twist silver wire and small beads into tendrils, leaves and birds, and join them with open, visible solder.
Draw the form from a natural plant or a medieval jewel: a hawthorn, a peacock, a pomegranate.
Sign the piece with the maker's mark, not a factory mark.
Keep each piece to one idea and to two or three materials.
anti_patterns: Gloss and exact edges that hide the hand

silhouette.shape: A medium pendant, buckle or necklace of open work: a central drop hung in a chain of links, with small leaves and beads.
silhouette.line: Soft, hand-drawn and slightly uneven; curves taken from a plant, with a small bead at each end of a wire.
silhouette.fit: Worn on a loose dress, a smock or a high-waist gown, on a long chain at the chest.
silhouette.proportion: A pendant is 4 to 8 cm tall on a 40 to 50 cm chain; a belt buckle is 8 to 12 cm wide.
rules: Hang a pendant on a chain of hand-made links of unequal size.
Set a single moonstone or opal in a bezel with a wire border.
Apply enamel in a small panel and fire it on silver.
Mark each piece with the maker's initials on the back.

fabrics.rule: Use silver, copper and enamel for the metal, and soft cabochon stones for the colour; show the hammer on the metal.

methods: open wire tendrils with visible solder
hand-made chain links of unequal size
construction.closures: A simple hook and eye, a hand-made hook clasp or a pin; a buckle with a tongue.
construction.details: A peacock, a leaf or a bird as the motif, a blue-green enamel panel, a tiny pearl drop and a maker's mark.

surface.pattern: Wire tendrils, leaves and birds on an open ground; no repeat, no machine border.
surface.gloss: Low to medium: hammered silver of 20 to 50 GU, with a dull oxide in the recesses and a bright enamel.
surface.wear: Silver tarnishes and the oxide darkens; the maker's marks soften with wear, which the style accepts.

palette.strategy: Soft silver and blue-green enamel, with the muted colours of moonstone, opal and turquoise.

processes: enamel firing in a small kiln
cabochon setting in a plain bezel
making.scale: Guilds and small studios, with one to twenty workers; each piece made by one hand from a drawing.
making.signs: Hammer marks, file marks, visible solder, uneven links and a maker's mark.

pieces.form: Silver pendant with a moonstone and a pearl drop
Open silver necklace with enamel leaves
Peacock brooch in silver and blue-green enamel
Silver ring with a cabochon opal in a plain bezel
Hammered copper cuff with a beaten edge

positive: moonstone cabochon in a plain bezel

canonical_works.work: Silver and enamel necklaces of the Guild

evidence.title: Sanctuary Pendant - Phoebe Anna Traquair - ABDAG008875

emotion.target_response: A warm, honest feeling: the viewer sees the maker's hand and a piece that is made to be worn, not shown.

use_cases: costume design for an Edwardian artist or a suffragette
a museum label for a guild piece
an image prompt for hand-made period jewels
avoid_when: the brief wants a flawless, machine finish
the brief is a diamond and platinum parure

modifiers.how: Add plique-a-jour enamel, a whiplash line and a woman's head or an insect; keep the hand work.
Remove the nature motif and the enamel, use a sharp, abstract form and keep the hand-made silver.

ornament_level.note: Ornament comes from wire and enamel, not from stones.
